schema.src: Stable slug identifying this entry — the source file's basename under todo/ without the .md extension (e.g. "value-affine-normal-form"). Used to reference this entry from another entry's deps, parent or closed_by. Never changes once another entry can point at it.
schema.title: String. The GitHub issue title: the source file's H1 heading verbatim in voice (a complaint is fine, not converted to an imperative), except that no R<digit> requirement number survives.
schema.state: String, either "open" or "closed" — whether the port script files the issue open or already closed.
schema.body: Array of pointer objects the port script resolves and concatenates in order at execute time; never prose written by the coder. Each element is one of {"file": "todo/x.md"} (whole file), {"file": "todo/x.md", "section": "heading text"} (one carved section), {"git": "<rev>:todo/x.md"} (a body that survives only in history), or {"text": "..."} (a short inline addition, e.g. a table row).
schema.provenance: String. A one-line note for the reviewer on how this entry's title/body/labels were derived — which source file, section or tier it came from, and any rewrite the script must perform (such as an R-number excision). Never a copy of the source's own prose.
schema.labels: Array of GitHub label name strings. Every entry carries "claude-code", exactly one "size/*" matching the size field below, and at least one "pkg/*" ("pkg/delayed-sampling", "pkg/gravensteiner", or both). "decision" is added where the item closes by recording a decision rather than by a diff.
schema.milestone: Integer 1-8, the # column of the plan's milestone table. Exactly one on every open entry; null (absent) on a closed entry.
schema.milestone_rationale: String or null. Free-text justification for the milestone choice, populated only where the assignment is genuinely arguable; null otherwise.
schema.size: String, one of "size/S" (one revision), "size/M" (one arc), or "size/L" (multiple arcs; may need subdivision, research, a maintainer design decision, or user testing). Mirrors the size/* string already present in labels.
schema.size_evidence: String. A verbatim quote from the source file that motivated the size, or exactly the literal string "no cue in source file" when there is none — in which case size takes the larger of the two candidate sizes considered.
schema.deps: Array of other entries' src strings that this entry depends on, i.e. must land first. Drives the Project board's top-to-bottom order.
schema.parent: The src string of this entry's parent entry, or null. Becomes a native GitHub sub-issue relation (used for the machinery entries filed under the v1-model specification entry).
schema.closed_by: String naming the revision that closed this item (short hash and subject), or a plain statement that none could be identified, for a closed entry; null for an open entry.
schema.issue: Integer GitHub issue number once the port script has created it, or null before that. The port script's resume marker — a non-null issue is never recreated.

entries.title: Nothing discrete exists, so the cultivar identity cannot be a node
entries.provenance: Whole file todo/discrete-nodes-and-dirichlet-categorical.md; README's discrete-path table. The file names an open carrier-representation fork (index-based vs. name-based categorical) that it flags as worth settling early.
entries.size_evidence: One carrier question worth settling early: should the categorical be `Distribution Int` with the caller maintaining an index-to-`Name` mapping, or `Distribution Name` with the weights carried alongside?

entries.title: A finite discrete latent should be enumerated, not sampled
entries.size_evidence: A recorded decision on whether (2) or (3) is worth pursuing, with (3)'s combinatorial cost stated.

entries.title: Only `Normal` is usable, and only the normal-normal conjugate pair delays
entries.provenance: Whole file todo/conjugate-pairs-beyond-normal.md; README's discrete-path table. The file deliberately groups several conjugate pairs in one document since each needs the same extension points.
entries.milestone_rationale: The normal-inverse-gamma pair is genuinely tied to milestone 1: README's shortlist calls this file's Gamma/inverse-gamma "needed by" cultivar-descriptions-are-not-observations' remaining conjugate-update wiring, which the same shortlist says is needed before literature ingestion, i.e. milestone 1's own "conjugate elicitation" clause. Kept at 6 anyway because the entry as filed bundles four pairs, not just that one, and its own Dirichlet-categorical row depends on vector-valued-variables-and-dirichlet and discrete-nodes-and-dirichlet-categorical (both milestone 6, see deps) — so the entry as a whole cannot close before other milestone-6 work does regardless of which pair is landed first. Splitting the file into one issue per pair so the elicitation half alone could move to milestone 1 is out of this todo's scope (one entry per file); the milestone-1 tie surfaces instead via todo 2's dependency from cultivar-descriptions-are-not-observations onto this entry.
entries.size_evidence: For each pair: a `Distribution` constructor; clauses in `pdf`, `sampleMarginal`, `marginalizeDistribution` and `conditionDist`; and a statistical acceptance test in the style of the existing ones

entries.title: No SMC integration — the paper's whole payoff is unrealised
entries.provenance: Whole file todo/no-smc-integration.md; README's discrete-path table.
entries.milestone_rationale: Grouped under README's discrete-path table with the rest of this batch, but the file's own argument is that a collapsed sweep can reach milestone 6's bar without SMC — this is the paper's payoff and a streaming-deployment want, not a hard requirement of "the real v1 network runs". Milestone 6 is still the best fit of the eight rungs; flagged as the one item in this batch that could plausibly slip later instead.
entries.size_evidence: So the deliverable is not "call `smc`" — it is deciding how a resampling step transports the analytic graph, and making that the documented composition.
